title: Lines: Slope & Equations
summary: A line's slope $m=\dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}$ measures steepness. Write lines in slope-intercept $y=mx+b$ or point-slope $y-y_1=m(x-x_1)$ form. Parallel lines share a slope; perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals.

slope.plain: Rise over run — steepness of a line.

slope-intercept form.in_class: Reads off slope and intercept directly.

point-slope form.in_class: Build a line from a point and a slope.

parallel lines.plain: Lines that never meet — same slope.

perpendicular lines.plain: Lines meeting at a right angle.

concept_sections.heading: Slope
concept_sections.explanation: Slope is the ratio of vertical change to horizontal change between two points: $m=\dfrac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}$. Positive rises, negative falls, zero is flat, undefined is vertical.

concept_sections.heading: Slope-intercept form
concept_sections.explanation: $y=mx+b$ shows the slope $m$ and $y$-intercept $b$ at a glance — the easiest form for graphing and reading behavior.

concept_sections.heading: Point-slope form
concept_sections.explanation: Given a point $(x_1,y_1)$ and slope $m$, write $y-y_1=m(x-x_1)$. Convert to slope-intercept if desired.

concept_sections.heading: Parallel and perpendicular
concept_sections.explanation: Parallel lines share the same slope; perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals ($m$ and $-1/m$).
math_steps: Perpendicular: flip and negate the slope.
Use with a point to build the line.

concept_sections.heading: Finding a line from two points
concept_sections.explanation: Compute the slope from the two points, then use point-slope with either point to get the equation.

real_world_examples.title: Cost with a flat fee
real_world_examples.scenario: A plan charges a base fee plus per-unit cost.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Total cost is linear: $y=mx+b$, with $b$ the fee and $m$ the rate.

real_world_examples.title: Road grade
real_world_examples.scenario: A highway sign shows a percent grade.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Grade is slope — rise over run — expressed as a percentage.

real_world_examples.title: Depreciation
real_world_examples.scenario: An asset loses value at a steady rate.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Its value is a line with negative slope; the intercept is the purchase price.
